title: Lift the ~10,000-primitive ortho depth budget per 2D frame

description:
A 2D frame can draw only about 10,000 primitives before the rest vanish without an error.

Every SDF draw (circle, line, rounded rect, glyph quad) calls Camera2D.incZIndex, which moves the next primitive ShaderProgram.ORTHO_Z_INCREMENT = 0.1 deeper. The ortho projection's far plane is ShaderProgram.ORTHO_FAR = 1000. After 1000 / 0.1 = 10,000 draws the z passes the far plane and the GPU clips every later draw. The descending far cursor (resetZIndex / decFarZIndex, starting at ORTHO_FAR - increment) uses up the same range from the other end, and each Camera2D.setZIndex(camera) adds 1 (10 draws' worth).

Found in CRAW-111's e-means playground (EMeansPlaygroundScene). Drawing 6000 sample points per panel, the left panel used up the whole budget, so the right panel, the MSE chart and all the text disappeared. The scene was cut to 1500 points per panel to fit. Its per-frame draws are 2 × points per panel + up to 2 × 700 Voronoi edges + 2 × k centroids + the chart segments + the text.

Ways to lift it, cheapest first:
1. Smaller increment or deeper far plane. 0.01 gives ~100,000 primitives; check that the depth buffer still separates layers at that spacing.
2. Advance depth per layer, not per primitive. Primitives in one flat layer (a point cloud, a set of edges) never need to sort against each other, so they can share one z.
3. Batched or instanced draws: one draw call per point cloud or edge set. This also fixes speed, since 10k separate SDF draws per frame is slow anyway.

Decision (the user, after a first pass with opt-in flat layers): option 3, automatic instanced batching. Circles and lines that share a shader and uniforms are queued and each run of consecutive draws goes out as one instanced draw with per-instance data, one depth step per run. It is not opt-in: it happens behind the existing SDF draw calls, so every 2D scene gets it, and a GL without instancing falls back to the per-primitive path. The flat-layer API from the first pass is removed.
definition-of-done:
1. Instanced batching is on by default for every 2D scene: SDFCircle and solid SDFLine draws queue as instanced runs behind the existing draw calls, with no scene opting in, and a GL without instancing falls back to the per-primitive path.
2. A 2D frame can draw well over 10,000 primitives (at least 50,000 circles) with all of them visible, including whatever is drawn after them; the unit test with 50,000 circles holds.
3. EMeansPlaygroundScene draws at least 6000 sample points per panel with both panels, the chart and the text visible; screenshot under tmp/. With 12,000+ points per panel it draws at a measured frame rate well above the per-primitive path's, before and after recorded in tmp/eng-41-measurements.json.
4. Existing 2D scenes (MainScene knot view, DSL graph view, IrregularGridScene, TradeScene) render the same as master: screenshot differences are no larger than between two master runs.
5. The far-plane warning stays: Camera2D.incZIndex logs "Camera2D: ortho depth past the far plane" once per frame when a draw or run lands past ORTHO_FAR.
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: a camera that records z per draw gives 50,000 draws z values all inside the near..far range.
2. A test scene, or the playground at n large, draws 50,000 circles then a text label; the screenshot shows the label.
3. Screenshots of the four existing 2D scenes before and after, compared with ixdar-cli image-diff.
changes-made: Chose option 2 (depth per layer): Camera2D.beginFlatLayer()/endFlatLayer() make every draw between them share one z and step one increment past the layer at the end. Each SDF draw is flushed on its own and the depth test is LEQUAL, so equal-z primitives keep painter's order; a flat layer costs one depth step however many primitives it holds. Option 1 rejected: over the -1000..1000 ortho range a 16-bit depth buffer (common WebGL default) resolves about 0.03 units, so 0.01 steps would collapse, and it only moves the cap to 100,000. Option 3 not needed for the DoD.
Camera2D.incZIndex logs once per frame when a draw used a z past ShaderProgram.ORTHO_FAR and sets the public depthBudgetExhausted flag; resetZIndex re-arms it (DoD 2).
EMeansPlaygroundScene: DRAWN_POINTS 1500 -> 6000 per panel; each side's sample points, Voronoi edges and centroids, and the chart curves, are drawn as flat layers.

New unit test ixdar-app/test/unit/render/Camera2DDepthBudgetTest: 50,000 circles in a flat layer plus a label after them all inside near..far with the label in front; per-primitive draws past the far plane set depthBudgetExhausted, and resetZIndex clears it.

Superseded at the user's request: the opt-in Camera2D.beginFlatLayer/endFlatLayer API and its calls in EMeansPlaygroundScene are removed; the user chose automatic instanced batching (option 3) instead.

New InstancedSdfShader (graphics/render/shaders) with sdf_circle_instanced.vs/.fs and sdf_line_instanced.vs/.fs: per-instance rows (circle: centre, radius, depth, fill, border colour, border thickness, edge; line: both ends, width, depth, both colours, edge). Consecutive draws through one instanced program and camera form a run: one depth step (camera.incZIndex at the run's start), one glDrawArraysInstanced. ShaderDrawable.draw queues SDFCircle and solid SDFLine (stock LineSDF shader) draws there by default; dashed/arrow/custom-shader lines, rounded rects, glyphs and the rest keep the per-primitive path.
Draw order is kept by flushing the pending run in ShaderProgram.use() (every other program's draw), before Camera2D/Camera3D viewport changes, and after drawScene in Scene.paintGL.
GL gains supportsInstancing/vertexAttribDivisor/drawArraysInstanced (LwjglGL: GL31/GL33; WebGL: WebGL2 via JSBody, detected at runtime); without instancing the per-primitive path runs as before.

Measured headless (tmp/eng-41-measurements.json): playground at 12,000 points per panel 18.7 fps on master (per-primitive) vs 44.9 fps instanced; 50,000 circles 42.8 fps. Trade and irregular-grid scenes pixel-identical to master; knot-view and DSL-graph diffs are the FPS readout and node run-time heat colours, smaller than master-vs-master.
review-summary: Every 2D scene's SDF circles and solid lines are now drawn in instanced runs, one depth step per run, with a once-per-frame warning past the far plane. Before, each primitive took its own depth step and draw call, so a frame silently lost everything after about 10,000 primitives.
